'''Jack Melton "John" Boardman''' (September 8, 1932 – May 29, 2025) was an American physicist. He was a professor of physics and astronomy at [[Queens College, City University of New York|Queens College]] and then [[Brooklyn College]] (where he spent the majority of his career) in [[New York City]]; an internationally renowned [[science fiction]] [[science fiction fandom|fan]], author and [[science fiction fanzines|fanzine publisher]]; and a [[board games|gaming authority]].

== Academic career ==
Boardman received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1952 and his [[Master of Science|M.S.]] from [[Iowa State University]] in 1956. He then attended [[Florida State University]] to begin his doctoral studies. However, he was expelled in 1957 due to his involvement with the [[Inter-Civic Council]] and more specifically for inviting three Black [[Florida A&M University]] [[exchange student]]s to a Christmas party.<ref>[http://www.tallahassee.com/legacy/special/boycott/profiles.html "The Ride to Equality: Fifty years after the Tallahassee bus boycott"], ''[[Tallahassee Democrat]]'' May 21, 2006 (special section)</ref><ref>[http://www.floridamemory.com/items/show/35174 Photograph: "Civil rights activists - Tallahassee, Florida" (195?) Image #RC12794 in series: "Reference collection", at ''Florida Memory'', Institute of Museum and Library Services, Division of Library and Information Services], [[Secretary of State of Florida|Florida Department of State]]</ref>

He ultimately received his [[Ph.D.]] in physics from [[Syracuse University]] in 1962; his [[doctoral thesis]] was titled ''[[Quantization (physics)|Quantization]] of the [[General Theory of Relativity]]''.<ref>[http://www.osti.gov/energycitations/product.biblio.jsp?osti_id=4679622 Bibliographic Citation: "QUANTIZATION OF THE GENERAL THEORY OF RELATIVITY" Energy Citations Database accessed March 23 2011]</ref> His publications include "Spherical Gravitational Waves" (a collaboration with his advisor, [[Peter Bergmann]], who had served as research assistant to [[Albert Einstein]] between 1936 and 1941),<ref>[https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.115.1318 Boardman, John and Bergmann, Peter G. "Spherical Gravitational Waves" ''Physical Review'' Volume 115, Issue 5 (September 1959); pp. 1318–1324]</ref> "Contributions to the Quantization Problem in General Relativity",<ref>[http://jmp.aip.org/resource/1/jmapaq/v6/i11/p1696_s1?isAuthorized=no Boardman, John. "Contributions to the Quantization Problem in General Relativity" ''Journal of Mathematical Physics'' Vol. 6, Issue 11 (1965), pp. 1696 ''et seq.''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320062155/http://jmp.aip.org/resource/1/jmapaq/v6/i11/p1696_s1?isAuthorized=no |date=2012-03-20 }}</ref> and "The Normal Modes Of A Hanging Oscillator Of Order ''N''".<ref>[http://www.fq.math.ca/17-1.html Boardman, John. ""The Normal Modes Of A Hanging Oscillator Of Order ''N''" ''Fibonacci Quarterly'' Vol. 17, Issue 1 (February 1979); pp. 37-39]</ref>

== Boardman and gaming ==
Boardman was involved in early [[Play-by-mail game|play-by-mail]] (PBM) for the ''[[Diplomacy (game)|Diplomacy]]'' game, and for a small fee he would send copies of each player's turns to every other player involved in a game.<ref name="designers">{{Cite book|author=Shannon Appelcline|title=Designers & Dragons|publisher=[[Mongoose Publishing]]|year=2011| isbn= 978-1-907702-58-7|pages=34}}</ref> He was one of the most noted figures in the game of Diplomacy, having established the original play-by-mail setup in 1961, and also the system of numbering each game for statistical purposes. These numbers, known as Boardman Numbers, include the year and a letter indicating sequence.<ref name="atoz">{{cite web | last = Reynolds | first = Harold | title = B Entries | work = Diplomacy A-Z, Version 6.0 | date = 2008-12-02 | url = http://www.badpets.net/Diplomacy/AtoZ/B.html | accessdate = 2008-12-22}}</ref>  For instance, 2004A was the first game started in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diplomatic-pouch.org/Zine/S1997M/Fitzpatrick/Bnumbers.html|title=A Short History of the Boardman Numbers|last=Walker|first=Rod|website=Diplomatic Pouch|date=1997|orig-year=1975-03-13|access-date=2017-07-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://archive.org/download/Liasons_Dangereuses_54-1975-03-12/Liasons_Dangereuses_54-1975-03-12.pdf|title=A Short History of the Boardman Numbers |last=Walker |first=Rod  |magazine=Liaisons Dangereuses |date=1975-03-13 |orig-year=1972|access-date=2017-07-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diplomatic-pouch.org/Zine/S1997M/Fitzpatrick/Numbers.html|title=Boardman and Miller Numbers|website=Diplomatic Pouch|date=1997|access-date=2017-07-03}}</ref>

Boardman started the first successful postal [[Diplomacy (game)|Diplomacy]] [[zine]], ''Graustark'', in 1963 as an offshoot from his [[science fiction fanzines|science fiction fanzine]] ''Knowable''.<ref name="atoz" />  Soon ''Graustark'' grew from just a gameturn-report newsletter to a hobby activity similar to [[science fiction]] [[fanzine]]s.<ref name="Encyc_Zines">Meinel, Jim. ''Encyclopedia of Postal Diplomacy Zines''. Great White North Productions, Alaska, USA, 1992.</ref> Boardman continued to produce ''Graustark'' for almost 50 years, publishing issue 793 in June 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.whiningkentpigs.com/DW/graustark.htm |title=Graustark Zine Archive |date=2014-06-02 |access-date=2017-07-03 |website=The Whining Kent Pigs |last=Kent |first=Douglas |archive-date=2016-08-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160805152349/http://www.whiningkentpigs.com/DW/graustark.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Science fiction ==
Boardman was long an active member of [[science fiction fandom]], famed for his strong political opinions; and has been the subject of at least two [[filk music|filksongs]]: "To John Boardman in Brooklyn"<ref>[http://www.massfilc.org/filkindex/nesfa.xml Index to the NESFA Hymnal]</ref> and "All Hail to the Fan John B." In addition to ''Knowable'', his [[science fiction fanzine]]s have included ''Dagon'' and ''Anakreon''. He also wrote at least two published [[fantasy]] stories, "Colon the Conqueror" (a [[Conan the Barbarian]] parody), published in the May 1958 issue of ''[[Fantastic Universe]]''; and "The Testament of Snefru", published in the 1980 anthology ''[[The Spell of Conan]]'' ([[L. Sprague de Camp]], ed.).

=== "The Asteroid Light" ===
Boardman's 1961 [[filk music|filksong]], "The Asteroid Light" (to the tune of the sea chanty "[[Eddystone Light]]") has been reprinted repeatedly, in venues ranging from science fiction anthologies (the 1972 anthology ''Futures Conditional'') to ''[[Sing Out]]'' magazine (V. 9, #1, p.&nbsp;24) to collections of protest music ([[Tom Glazer|Glazer, Tom]]. ''Songs of Peace, Freedom and Protest''. New York: David McKay, 1970). It has also frequently been discussed in papers on filk music.<ref>[http://cfmb.icaap.org/content/23.2/BV23-2part2.pdf Fowke, Edith. "Filksongs as Modern Folk Songs". ''Canadian Folklore Canadien'' (Vol. 7; 1985)]</ref><ref>Titus, A. Costandina & Simich, Jerry L. "From 'atomic bomb baby' to 'nuclear funeral': Atomic music comes of age, 1945-1990" ''Popular Music and Society'', Vol. 14, #4 (Winter 1990), pp. 11-37</ref><ref>Simpson, Claude M., Jr. "Review: [untitled]" ''[[Western Folklore]]'', Vol. 21, #4 (Oct., 1962), pp. 290-291</ref>

He also wrote a regular column, "Science for Science Fiction", for the first twelve issues of [[Ares (magazine)|''Ares'']] magazine.

== Personal life and death ==
{{Citation needed section|date=May 2025}}
After having been a resident of the [[Flatbush, Brooklyn|Flatbush]] neighborhood of [[Brooklyn, New York]] since 1969 (his family's longtime home at 234 East 19th Street in the [[Beverley Squares|Beverley Square East]] subsection was used as a set in fellow Brooklynite [[Spike Lee]]'s [[Malcolm X (1992 film)|''Malcolm X'']]), Boardman primarily lived in the [[Washington metropolitan area]] (including a long stint in [[Frederick, Maryland]]) beginning in the early 2010s due to the presence of nearby family and increasingly paramount health exigencies. His wife, Perdita Lilly Nelson Girsdansky, who was previously married to [[Ray Nelson (author)|Ray Nelson]], died on November 26, 2017 after a long battle with [[dementia]].

Boardman died in his sleep in [[Montgomery Village, Maryland]], on May 29, 2025, at the age of 92.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=John Melton Boardman Obituary (2025) - Millersville, MD - Maryland Cremation Services |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/john-boardman-obituary?id=58519771 |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref>
